title: What anytype actually does when it is re-typed at run time
instruction: In the sandbox model, settle a language claim with a RUNTIME test rather than by reading. The claim in circulation is that an `anytype` takes the type of its first assignment and cannot then hold a different type. Write a SysTest class that measures it instead of asserting it from memory. (1) Scaffold with generate_object(mode="pattern", pattern="systest", attributes=["SysTestGranularity(SysTestGranularity::Unit)", "SysTestCheckInTest"]). (2) Write four methods, each using typeOf(...) as the observation and comparing with enum2Str so a failure message names the type: a local anytype reports the type it was given; the SAME local accepts a str after an int; a class MEMBER of type anytype accepts the same change (this is where the folklore is usually told); and an anytype returned from a method keeps its type across the boundary. (3) Build and run with run_systest_class. Do NOT write the assertions to match what you expect — write them to report what happens, run, and let the result decide what the knowledge entry says. That is the whole point of an R-only case.
